needs: heat exchanged between two things, weighted by mass and amount, drawing the source down
contents (S8): water in the hide keeping it wet and capping its temperature
shock that reads S15 and is independent of how time is cut into acts
a boiling threshold and steam as events
move (carrying stones with tongs)
note: Derives: stones take minutes to heat (2.3 after 1 min, 4.9 after 30) and do not burn; a hot stone burns a bare hand and does not light green tongs; with the caller issuing heat both ways the stones shed heat fast, one batch leaves the water at 2.6 and it passes 4.5 on the tenth; a soaked hide will not light in a flame that lights it dry. RULE ERRORS, all in heat.ts: (1) heat() never cools the source and reads no amounts, so one stone left in a hide full of water takes it to 4.9, and a cupful with four stones heats exactly as a hide full with one; the general rule is an exchange toward a balance weighted by mass times amount. (2) `drying` runs whatever the source is and ignition() asks only how hot the source is, so a hide holding boiling water for an hour dries to 0 and catches fire, and water at 4.2 lights dry kindling (ignition point 3.8); a liquid source should wet rather than dry, and only a burning or glowing source should light. (3) shock() tests the drop within one act against 2: five minutes in the water as one act cracks the stone, as five acts of one minute never does; it should depend on the rate of change, not the act's length. Also shock never reads flaw, so every stone of this row cracks on every long plunge where the scenario makes it the flawed one.

note: RULE ERROR in load.ts strength(): a long support's section is size minus 2 whatever the direction of the load, so a sound thin stick (strength 2.1) snaps under half a heavy flat stone (weight 3) and the trap cannot be set; a prop borne along its length should bear far more than the same stick as a beam. Confidence is low: the mass scale is coarse and with the slab at mass 3 it would hold. The fall derives as a deep crushing wound that bleeds little (depth 2.8, bleeding 0.8), but it does not kill: health stays 4.8 because a wound costs health only through bleeding, and a lighter animal cannot be told from a fox because every body is the same flesh. Baiting, the careful theft and the reset are out of reach; the chain breaks at step 1.

needs: S3 'starved of air it chars': going out for lack of air keeps the remaining fuel, as a charred element (a charsTo beside burnsTo)
air at the level of the thing or a cover relation (R5, R6), so a seal can be partial and leak

a glowing-coals stage of burning
note: Derives: split wood lights and burns away in the open in about an hour (fuel 60) to ash, and with no air it stops flaming. RULE ERROR in drift.ts: the burning drift sets fuel to 0 when the place's air is 0, and driftThing reads 'was burning of self, now is not' as burned away, so wood sealed with thirty minutes of fuel left is consumed whole and replaced by ash in the first step: smothering destroys exactly what it should save. The general rule: only fuel running out consumes; going out for lack of air leaves what had not burned, charred. The partial leak in step 4 needs air per thing, not per place.

needs: phase change for liquids (S6 from S1: water freezing and thawing)
P22 swell pushing on what holds it, checked by Load against strength and S15
flaw growing under repeated sub-critical load (a crack widening per cycle)
contents for a crack that holds water
note: Derives: the rock takes the poured water as a film, rock and water reach 0 by morning, and one night does not split it. RULE ERROR in drift.ts, the wetness drift: film drying reads warmth only above mild (exposed = 1 + max(0, T - 2) + wind), so the water in the crack has dried to 0 by morning at freezing, as fast as on a mild day; drying should slow toward nothing as temperature falls to freezing and stop for ice. Beyond that the chain breaks at step 2: isLiquid() is true for a liquid element at any temperature so nothing freezes, and nothing reads swell, so there is no wedge, no widening and no freeze-thaw count. Medium confidence because the water is encoded as wetness on the rock; with contents it might not be exposed to drying at all.

note: Derives: ten minutes of searching the bank turns up clay (yield 2.2) and none on the trail; the plug is still soft after an hour in the sun, dry and set within a day (wetness 0.4 at 18 h, set by 24 h), harder than it was, stiff (flexibility 1 or less) where the leather round it flexes (4), and wetting it again does not soften it (M5). The chain breaks at step 2: there is no plug in a hole, so neither the seal nor its cracking loose under flexing can happen; the mismatch the failure comes from is visible only as two numbers. Note that M5 makes sun-dried clay waterproof for good, which is true of fired clay and not of a dried plug.
